sources.entry: borgbackup - A deduplicating archiver with compression and encryption.

summary.one_liner: BorgBackup (Borg) is a deduplicating backup program with optional compression and authenticated encryption; this README is for the unstable Borg2 beta on the master branch.
summary.what_it_does: Borg splits files into variable-length chunks using content-defined chunking and stores only chunks not already in the repository, so repeated backups store only changes. Deduplication works across files, machines and archives sharing one repo, and does not depend on file names or timestamps staying the same. Data can be compressed with lz4, zstd, zlib or lzma, and encrypted client-side with AES-OCB or chacha20-poly1305, or authenticated-only modes. Repositories can live on remote hosts via ssh://, http(s)://, sftp://, s3://, b2:// or rclone:. Archives can be mounted as user-space filesystems for browsing and restoring. The README says single-file binaries are provided for Linux, macOS, FreeBSD and Windows (experimental).
use_cases: automated daily backups of home or server directories
off-site encrypted backups to untrusted storage
backing up virtual machine images or raw disks efficiently
browsing and restoring old backup archives as a filesystem
backing up to S3, B2, SFTP or rclone-supported cloud storage
notable: Content-defined chunking deduplication, with fastcdc as default chunker
Client-side authenticated encryption (AES-OCB, chacha20-poly1305) with HMAC-SHA256 or Blake3 hashing
Remote repositories over ssh, http(s), sftp, S3, B2 and rclone
caveats: Borg2 is in beta; the README says breaking changes occur between betas with no upgrade path, so repos must be recreated, and it should not be used for production backups
Some platforms (NetBSD, OpenBSD, illumos/Solaris) are install-from-source or package only, with partial xattr/ACL support
Windows, Cygwin and WSL support are marked experimental
